readme:
# LLaVA 视觉 Token 注入与标签对齐

## 1. 问题

实现 `pack_visual_tokens(text: Tensor, visual: Tensor, labels: Tensor, image_index: int) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]`。

单图单样本的视觉序列打包与监督标签对齐；输入特征已经投影，不实现视觉编码器、语言模型或训练数据构建。

## 2. 核心公式

$$
E=[E_{<i};V;E_{>i}],\qquad y=[y_{<i};\underbrace{-100,\ldots,-100}_{P};y_{>i}].
$$

## 3. 公式到代码

图像占位是打包指令，不是额外保留的 token。将其左右切片与视觉块拼接，标签使用相同切片边界。视觉 embedding 参与上下文计算，但没有对应的文本预测标签，因此置为 -100。concat 的反向传播自然把梯度分配回各来源，删除的占位不会影响输出。

## 4. 本题约定

单条序列：text=[T,D] 包含一枚图像占位，visual=[P,D] 是已投影特征，labels=[T] int64。用全部 P 个视觉 token 替换 image_index 处的一个 token；视觉标签填 -100，保留其它原标签。返回长度 T+P-1 的 embedding 与 labels。梯度流向保留文本及视觉，删除的占位梯度为零。

CPU float32/float64；不得修改输入；仅接受有限浮点值。测试包含独立 oracle、边界、适用的梯度检查，以及被测函数参与的实验。

## 5. 交互图

确定性 CPU 实验调用被测函数；图表展示实际优化、检索或分组行为，请结合 metrics 阅读。合成实验不代表论文的完整基准结果。

## 6. 在网页中运行

在右侧 Python 编辑器中补全实现，点击 **运行测试**。查看失败测试的原因、期望值与实际值，修改代码后再次运行。所有必要测试通过后，题目会标记为已完成并解锁坑点讲解。

## 7. 延伸

阅读下面来源的对应机制，再将独立核扩展到论文完整架构和数据管线。本题使用上面明确列出的可判题范围与教学简化。

import math
import torch
from torch import Tensor
import torch.nn.functional as F


def _floating(*values):
    first = values[0]
    for value in values:
        if not value.is_floating_point() or value.dtype != first.dtype or value.device != first.device or not torch.isfinite(value).all():
            raise ValueError("floating inputs must be finite and share dtype/device")

def pack_visual_tokens(text: Tensor, visual: Tensor, labels: Tensor, image_index: int) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    _floating(text,visual)
    if text.ndim!=2 or visual.ndim!=2 or text.numel()==0 or visual.numel()==0 or text.shape[1]!=visual.shape[1] or labels.shape!=(text.shape[0],) or labels.dtype!=torch.long or not 0<=image_index<text.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("expected nonempty compatible features, long labels and valid image index")
    packed=torch.cat((text[:image_index],visual,text[image_index+1:]),dim=0)
    ignored=torch.full((visual.shape[0],),-100,dtype=labels.dtype,device=labels.device)
    packed_labels=torch.cat((labels[:image_index],ignored,labels[image_index+1:]),dim=0)
    return packed,packed_labels

# LLaVA visual-token insertion and label alignment

## 1. Problem

Implement `pack_visual_tokens(text: Tensor, visual: Tensor, labels: Tensor, image_index: int) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]`.

Pack one image into one sample and align supervision labels; features are already projected, excluding the vision encoder, language model, and data construction.

## 2. Core equations

$$
E=[E_{<i};V;E_{>i}],\qquad y=[y_{<i};\underbrace{-100,\ldots,-100}_{P};y_{>i}].
$$

## 3. From equations to code

The placeholder is a packing instruction, not an extra retained token. Concatenate its left and right slices around the visual block, using identical label boundaries. Visual embeddings provide context but have no language targets, so their labels are -100. Concatenation routes gradients back to retained sources; the removed placeholder cannot affect the output.

## 4. Conventions

One sequence: text is [T,D] with one image placeholder, visual is projected [P,D], and labels is int64 [T]. Replace the token at image_index with all P visual tokens; fill their labels with -100 and retain all other labels. Return length T+P-1 embeddings and labels. Gradients reach retained text and visual features; the removed placeholder receives zero gradient.

CPU float32/float64; no input mutation. Finite inputs only. Tests use scalar oracles, boundary cases, appropriate gradient checks, and a submitted-function experiment.

## 5. Interactive figure

The deterministic CPU experiment calls your submitted function. The chart displays measured optimization, retrieval, or grouping behavior; inspect its metrics alongside the trace. Synthetic experiments do not reproduce paper benchmark scores.

## 6. Run your implementation

Complete the functions in the Python editor on the right, then click **Run tests**. Inspect each failed check, update your implementation, and run again. Passing every required check marks the problem as solved and unlocks the notes.

## 7. Extensions

Read the cited mechanism, then extend the isolated kernel to the paper’s complete architecture and data pipeline. The exercise fixes a narrow, testable contract; its teaching simplifications are stated above.
